name: Linear Regression
description: Linear regression is a fundamental supervised learning algorithm that models the relationship between a dependent variable (target) and one or more independent variables (features) by fitting a linear equation. It assumes the output is a linear combination of input features plus an error term.

concept.mathematicalFormulation: y = β₀ + β₁x₁ + β₂x₂ + ... + βₙxₙ + ε
concept.explanation: The algorithm finds coefficients (β) that minimize the difference between predicted and actual values. For simple linear regression (one feature): y = mx + b. The goal is to find the line of best fit through the data points.
assumptions: Linearity: Relationship between features and target is linear
Independence: Observations are independent of each other
No multicollinearity: Features are not highly correlated

idealScenarios: Small to medium datasets with linear relationships
avoidWhen: Categorical target variables (use logistic regression instead)
Outliers that significantly affect the line

fitIntercept.impact: If False, regression line passes through origin

regularization.impact: Prevents overfitting by penalizing large coefficients

alpha.impact: Higher values = stronger regularization, simpler model

training: Fit model on training data using OLS (Ordinary Least Squares)
interpretation: Coefficients represent change in target per unit change in feature

complexity.scalability: Excellent - works well with large datasets

variants.polynomialRegression: Extends linear regression by adding polynomial terms
